message.content:
Here’s a quick, ready‑to‑run example that shows how to fetch the first 20 comments for the domain **microsoft.com** using your API key (`gamma_key`).  
Feel free to copy‑paste it into your terminal (or adapt it to your preferred language).

---

## 1️⃣ Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.zenrows.com/v1/comments?domain=microsoft.com&limit=20" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer gamma_key"
```

### What this does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `https://api.zenrows.com/v1/comments` | Base endpoint for comments |
| `?domain=microsoft.com` | Filters comments to the specified domain |
| `&limit=20` | Returns only the first 20 results |
| `-H "Authorization: Bearer gamma_key"` | Passes your API key in the HTTP header |

> **Tip:** If you prefer to pass the key as a query parameter instead of a header, you can do:
> ```bash
> curl -X GET "https://api.zenrows.com/v1/comments?domain=microsoft.com&limit=20&key=gamma_key"
> ```

---

## 2️⃣ Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.zenrows.com/v1/comments"
params = {
    "domain": "microsoft.com",
    "limit": 20
}
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer gamma_key"
}

response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
print(response.json())
```

---

## 3️⃣ Sample Response (truncated)

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "12345",
      "comment": "Great product!",
      "author": "John Doe",
      "date": "2024-07-01T12:34:56Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "12346",
      "comment": "Could use better support.",
      "author": "Jane Smith",
      "date": "2024-07-02T09:21:30Z"
    }
    /* ... up to 20 items ... */
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total": 57,
    "limit": 20,
    "offset": 0
  }
}
```

> **Note:** The actual fields (`id`, `comment`, `author`, `date`, etc.) may vary depending on the API’s schema. Check the official documentation for the exact structure.

---

## 4️⃣ Quick Checklist

- ✅ Replace `gamma_key` with your real API key.
- ✅ Verify that the domain (`microsoft.com`) is correct.
- ✅ Adjust `limit` if you need more or fewer results.
- ✅ Handle pagination if you want to retrieve all comments (`offset`/`page` parameters).

That’s it! Once you run the command, you’ll receive a JSON payload containing up to 20 comments for the specified domain. Happy coding!
